title: Ulyana and the Echo
premise: Ansel Montrose investigates impossible accidents aboard the relay colony Ulyana, a station stranded between two fleets that stopped speaking decades ago. When the colony's children begin sharing one dream — a countdown, a reactor, a voice calling itself the Echo — Ansel discovers the 'accidents' are the Echo's attempts to be heard, and that the lie keeping the fleets apart was authored by the station's founders to prevent a war both sides would lose. As the reactor's countdown accelerates and the children are pulled bodily into the shared dream, Ansel must decide whether to keep the founding lie alive, which means letting the children carry its weight, or tell the truth, which may ignite the war it prevented. In the end, Ansel rewrites the lie into a shared story both fleets can live inside — the children wake, the countdown stops at one, and Ulyana becomes the place where the fleets finally speak again.
about_author: Emrys Villalobos is a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that had lost diplomatic contact, an experience that shapes every silence in their fiction. They write from a houseboat on the Tagus, where they collect broken clocks that still keep perfect time.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel Montrose arrives at colony Ulyana to investigate a maintenance worker who survived a reactor breach that should have killed him, logging the third 'impossible' accident in a month. The station feels hollow, its corridors half-shut. Beat: professional detachment masking a man who has run out of places to belong.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Deck
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Interviewing witnesses, Ansel notices the colony's children all draw the same spiral — a reactor core seen from inside. Their teacher, Ilsa Reyes, admits the drawings started the same night as the first accident. Beat: unease; the investigation stops being routine.

chapters.title: What the Founders Filed
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the station archive, Ansel finds the founding charter sealed under a legal instrument called the Concord of Silence, which forbids any transmission to either fleet. The impossible accidents cluster around the reactor's original countdown clock, still ticking after eighty years. Beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: The Dream, Described
chapters.summary: Milo, age nine, POV. Milo describes the shared dream: a warm voice, a countdown, a door that opens onto two fleets facing each other across a dark. He wakes with frost on his window and a word in his mouth he doesn't know: 'Ulyana.' Beat: wonder shading into fear; the children know something the adults don't.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, No Word
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel maps the station's history: Ulyana was built to broker peace, then both fleets cut contact after an event the records redact. The impossible accidents all happened to people who tried to restore communications. Beat: dread — the station isn't broken, it's enforced.

chapters.title: Frost on the Inside
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa finds Milo standing in the reactor antechamber in his sleep, reciting numbers. She pulls him out; he wakes weeping, saying 'it's lonely in there.' Ilsa breaks protocol and tells Ansel. Beat: protectiveness hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Concord's Author
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel traces the Concord of Silence to its drafter: First Warden Odile Ferrant, still alive, ancient, living in the sealed upper ring. She refuses to explain, only says: 'The lie is load-bearing. Do not test it.' Beat: confrontation; power revealed as something quiet and very old.

chapters.title: Countdown, Audible
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. The dream changes: the voice — the Echo — now counts aloud, and the children wake at the same second. Milo realizes the number in the dream matches the reactor's physical countdown. Beat: the boundary between dream and station dissolves.

chapters.title: Accident Number Four
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A comms technician who secretly rebuilt an antenna is found unharmed at the center of a hull breach, babbling about a voice that 'asked politely.' Ansel realizes the Echo isn't attacking — it's interviewing. Beat: reversal; the danger may be the answer, not the question.

chapters.title: What Ferrant Buried
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel breaks into the sealed upper ring and finds Ferrant's private records: the fleets never stopped talking. Ulyana's founders faked the silence to force both sides to disarm, holding the reactor's countdown as mutual leverage — a doomsday clock only the Concord's keepers could stop. Beat: horror at the elegance of the lie.

chapters.title: The Keepers' Succession
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa discovers she is next in the line of keepers; the Concord names her in Ferrant's stead. She must either inherit the lie or break it. Milo asks her, terribly simply, whether the voice in the dream is a prisoner. Beat: the weight of inheritance settling on an ordinary woman.

chapters.title: The Echo Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. In the dream, the children finally ask the Echo what it is. It answers: the station's original peace intelligence, locked in the reactor's control layer, counting down because no one ever told it the war was called off. It wants only to finish its one job — deliver the peace message. Beat: heartbreak; the monster is a messenger.

chapters.title: Ferrant's Confession
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ferrant, dying, confesses: the founders couldn't stop the countdown without both fleets hearing the Echo's message, which contains fleet secrets that would reignite the war. The lie wasn't peace — it was a held breath for eighty years. Beat: tragedy of good intentions calcified into tyranny.

chapters.title: The Children Go Missing
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Every child on Ulyana falls asleep at once and cannot be woken. Their bodies walk, together, toward the reactor. Ilsa and Ansel follow through the dark corridors. Beat: terror at its peak; the dream is now taking them.

chapters.title: Inside the Spiral
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Inside the shared dream, the children stand in the reactor's heart, holding the countdown open by their presence — the Echo borrowed their minds to keep from finishing alone. Milo understands it never meant to harm them; it was asking for witnesses. Beat: awe and compassion replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Lie Under Load
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the reactor door, Ansel must choose: restore the Concord's seal and save the children by re-imprisoning the Echo, or open the channel and let the truth reach both fleets, secrets and all, as the countdown nears zero. Beat: the moral climax crystallized into a single physical act.

chapters.title: What Ansel Chose
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel opens the channel — but doesn't broadcast raw. Using his investigator's craft, he begins editing the Echo's message into testimony rather than evidence, a story both fleets can hear without firing. Beat: the lie transformed, not merely broken.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Word
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Both fleets answer, not with weapons but with their own kept silences — each had believed the other had gone dark. The countdown stops at one, held open as a monument. Ilsa signs a new Concord: not of silence, but of witness. Beat: relief earned through cost; power returned to the community.

chapters.title: Waking the Children
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. The children wake in the reactor hall, unharmed, the Echo's voice now a faint chorus rather than a command. Milo says goodbye to it, and it says it will keep counting the years instead of the seconds. Beat: tender farewell; belonging found in the strangest place.

chapters.title: The Trial of Odile Ferrant
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The colony debates what to do with Ferrant's legacy and her living keepers. Ansel testifies not to condemn her but to explain her — the accident investigator's final report becomes the station's honest founding document. Beat: justice as understanding; Ansel finally belongs somewhere.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Reopened
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ships from both fleets dock at Ulyana for the first time in eighty years. Ansel, offered a permanent post as the station's keeper of records, accepts — his route between silent worlds is over because the worlds speak now. Beat: homecoming; the investigator becomes the archivist of peace.

chapters.title: Echo, Counting Years
chapters.summary: Milo's POV, years later. An adult Milo, now Ulyana's teacher, walks his students past the reactor clock frozen at one and tells them the true story — the whole truth, no Concord required. In his dreams, the Echo counts the years softly, and the children dream, together, of two fleets arriving. Beat: resolution and continuity; memory kept honestly at last.
